Bombastic

/bom-BAS-tik/ - rhymes with fantastic · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Bombastic means using inflated, self-important language with little substance.

The gym's bombastic radio spot promised 'a total rebirth of the human body'; the gym itself contained one treadmill and two mirrors.

Worked Example

The awards-show host grew more bombastic with every category: by midnight he was introducing a regional jingle contest as 'a turning point in the history of sound itself.'

Bombastic is more precise than 'exaggerated' or 'wordy' because it points at inflated, self-important language with nothing solid inside — the verbal equivalent of padding, all stuffing and no substance.

How Bombastic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

overblown

overblown: puffed past its true size, whether or not anyone is showing off

pompous

pompous: self-important in manner and tone overall, not only in language

grandiloquent

grandiloquent: reaches for lofty, high-flown words; bombastic adds the hollowness underneath

Antonyms

understated

understated: deliberately says less than it could

plainspoken

plainspoken: uses ordinary words for plain truths

How Strong Is It? — showy → flowery → bombastic

showy vs. bombastic

showy vs. bombastic: A showy phrase wants attention but can still be honest about its size — far milder than bombastic, which inflates the claim itself.

flowery vs. bombastic

flowery vs. bombastic: Flowery language piles on ornament, yet it stops short of bombastic: flowers decorate a real message, while bombast replaces the message with hot air.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — bombast

Root — bombast: cotton padding once used to stuff garments; inflated language

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of

Put it together

Put it together: Bombast (the cotton stuffing tailors once packed into doublets to make chests look grander) + -ic (characteristic of) = having the character of padding. Elizabethans watched padded speeches the way they watched padded shoulders, and the insult stuck: bombastic language is stuffed to look bigger than it is.

Use the root in a new word: bombast

Use the root in a new word: bombast: Strip the bombast from the manifesto and its whole program fits on an index card.

Word Choice

critical / vivid

Use bombastic to mock language that inflates itself — campaign promises, trailer voice-overs. Plain 'exaggerated' overstates facts; bombastic overdresses them. Its unit-mates mark the poles: laconic speech barely opens its mouth, prosaic speech is flat but honest, and bombastic speech booms about nothing.
